title: Rate limits & org/project keys demo with Medivance Health
summary: AE+SE walkthrough of Redwood rate limiting and multi-tenant controls focused on org/project API keys, quota scoping, burst handling and audit/logging. Customer had questions about per-project isolation, delegated keys for partners, and SAML/SSO integration. Agreed next steps: send security docs, pricing with dedicated quotas and a short pilot plan.
next_steps: Sofia to send security pack and org/project keys docs by 2026-04-22
Marcus to schedule a 1-hour technical deep dive benchmark session w/ Samir for week of 2026-04-27
Medivance to share expected QPS and peak token estimates before deep dive
action_items: Sofia Chen: Send security/compliance docs + pricing deck by 2026-04-22
Marcus Patel: Prep benchmark runbook and sample load script by 2026-04-24
Ethan Cole (Medivance): Share traffic profile and expected peaks by 2026-04-24
header:
Date: 2026-04-20 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE); Marcus Patel (Redwood SE); Avery Russell (Redwood CSM); Dr. Laura Gomez (Medivance); Ethan Cole (Medivance); Priya Nair (Medivance Sec); Samir Reddy (Medivance SRE)
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. we're gonna run through rate limits, org and project keys, and how you can use the console + api to manage quotas. quick intro from the medivance side?
[00:12] Dr. Laura (Medivance): hi, this is laura, i'm head of ai. we want to evaluate how to onboard multiple clinical teams and partners without leaking quotas between them. main concerns are data residency and strict audit trails.
[00:26] Ethan (Medivance): and hi, ethan here, platform eng. we'll run inference from a few services and need per-project keys so teams can auto-scale.
[00:33] Marcus (Redwood SE): great; quick note, i'll go deep on the console and api calls, and show how we model org-level quotas vs project-level limits.
[00:40] Sofia: feel free to interrupt. first slide - overview. we support org keys (scoped to account) and project keys (scoped per product/team). you can apply rate limits at both layers and set quotas (monthly token caps) per project.
[00:55] Priya (Medivance): when you say project keys, can these be rotated automatically? we need rotation for partners.
[01:02] Marcus: yes, keys are short-lived by default if you opt-in; we also have delegated keys for partners tied to an org role, and you can revoke per-key. we'll show the console flow.
[01:12] [01:15] screen share starts - Redwood console
[01:16] Marcus: here is the org panel, you can see org-wide quotas and usage. if you expand an org you'll see projects listed, each has its own rate limit settings - rps, burst, and monthly token caps. default is conservative but you can edit.
[01:30] [01:31] Dr. Laura: can we cap concurrent requests separately from rps? some of our models are long-running.
[01:37] Marcus: yes, we have concurrent request caps per project and also per-route. so you can have global rps 200 but project A concurrent 10 if it's latency-sensitive.
[01:45] Sofia: quick nuance - burst behavior: token bursts are allowed up to a burst window; we smooth with a token bucket so brief spikes don't immediately cause rejections, but sustained spikes will hit quota.
[01:58] Ethan: how does fallback work if a project hits quota? do requests fail or auto-fallback to smaller model?
[02:05] Marcus: configurable. by default we return 429 and an explanation header. you can configure automatic fallback policies that route to a lower-cost model (e.g., redwood-compat-7b) or route to a dedicated capacity pool if you have reserved capacity. there is also a retry-after.
[02:20] Priya: about billing segmentation - if project A goes over, will it charge the org or the project owner?
[02:26] Sofia: billing is tied to the org but we provide per-project cost allocation and usage reports. you can export granular token-level billing for showback/chargeback.
[02:36] [02:38] Marcus: now the api. sample request: POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/completions with an x-redwood-key header using the project key. the key scope determines allowed routes and quotas.
[02:51] [02:55] transcription glitch: "x redwood key" heard as "x red wood key" a couple times
[03:00] Marcus: for partner delegation we issue limited-scope keys that only allow embedding calls or only allow chat calls; scopes are enforced at the gateway.
[03:09] Dr. Laura: any limits on number of keys? we'll have dozens per partner.
[03:13] Marcus: no hard cap, but recommended practice is rotate and aggregate usage per partner. keys are listed and searchable in console.
[03:18] [03:20] screen: quota rule editor
[03:21] Marcus: here you can create a rule: e.g., project X max 10k tokens/min, burst 2k, monthly 5M tokens. rules can be based on routes, model families, and even tag labels.
[03:36] Samir (Medivance): how about enforcement latency - is there eventual consistency? we need near-real-time enforcement for safety-critical pipelines.
[03:44] Marcus: enforcement is immediate at the gateway; there is a short propagation window for new rules (a few seconds). for high-safety flows we recommend per-route caps plus synchronous checks.
[03:55] [04:00] Sofia: now i'll demo service accounts and audit logs.
[04:03] Sofia: service accounts are tied to org roles and can be constrained to projects; audit logs capture every authentication event, key issuance, and quota changes. logs are exportable to your SIEM via syslog or S3.
[04:15] Priya: is the audit information tamper-evident? we need chain of custody.
[04:20] Marcus: logs are signed and we support log shipping to your KMS-backed S3 and can enable retention policies. full audit trail with actor id, IP, and before/after for quota edits.
[04:34] Dr. Laura: what about private deployments? we run some workloads on-prem. does the org/project key model work in private?
[04:41] Sofia: yes, Private and Dedicated support same control-plane semantics; for private deployments you can choose to mirror control-plane metadata to your VPC or run with a hybrid control plane. some of the wording in our docs might say "mirror" but it's essentially the same concepts.
[04:55] Ethan: latency - if we put keys on edge services, will token bucket enforcement add extra hops?
[05:00] Marcus: enforcement happens at the ingress; overhead is minimal - a couple ms, it's on the critical path but optimized in C++ path. also we support local caches for quota tokens when you run Redwood Dedicated in a region to reduce RTT.
[05:12] [05:15] small cross-talk, someone asks for a quick example of API error payload
[05:18] Marcus: 429 response body includes {"code":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"project quota exceeded","retry_after":60} - i realize curly braces can be mis-transcribed but that's the payload.
[05:29] Priya: will the retry_after be seconds or an absolute timestamp?
[05:32] Marcus: seconds.
[05:34] Dr. Laura: we heard about KV cache earlier; can caching cause quota leakage between requests?
[05:40] Marcus: good question - we do prefix caching and KV cache for decoded tokens, but quotas are per-request accounting; cached responses don't bypass quota accounting if they are served from shared cache, we still record a token delta. sometimes transcription shows "K V cash" which is, uh, k v cache.
[05:56] [06:00] Sofia: switching to Optimize briefly - Optimize will analyze your traffic and recommend which projects to pin to quantized variants, suggest batching windows, and recommend org vs project quotas to minimize cost.
[06:12] Ethan: can Optimize recommend different models per workflow? e.g., clinician notes vs patient triage?
[06:16] Marcus: yes, Optimize uses workload labels and evaluates latency/quality tradeoffs; it can suggest a fallback model for heavy load.
[06:23] Priya: security - is key metadata stored encrypted?
[06:27] Marcus: yes, all key material is encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS if requested; we also offer HSM-backed signing for keys in enterprise plans.
[06:38] Dr. Laura: do you support SAML/SSO provisioning for org admins to issue keys?
[06:42] Sofia: yes, SAML + SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC roles control who can create org or project keys.
[06:48] [07:00] demo: creating a project key
[07:02] Marcus: click create key, choose project scope, check scopes (completions, embeddings), set expiry 30 days, optional usage cap (tokens). you can also select "rotate automatically" to generate a new key every N days and retire the old one.
[07:18] Dr. Laura: we'd like delegated keys for external partners with read-only embedding rights and a 1M token/month cap. can we enforce downstream partner rate limits?
[07:27] Marcus: yes, delegated keys plus per-key quotas enforce that. you can also tag keys and have alerting on high usage.
[07:34] Samir: does alerting integrate with pagerduty?
[07:36] Marcus: yes, alerting hooks to webhook, slack, pagerduty.
[07:40] [07:45] Sofia: let's talk about quotas during scale tests. if you run a spike test, we recommend provisioning a temporary higher quota or using a canary project with higher burst to validate.
[07:54] Ethan: for the pilot we want to simulate peak concurrency of 250 rps across 3 projects and sustained 100 rps for an hour. can you support that on hosted?
[08:03] Marcus: hosted can, but if you need guaranteed throughput we recommend Dedicated capacity; we can reserve a pool and set fallback policies so you don't hit 429s.
[08:13] Dr. Laura: what's the lead time for Dedicated?
[08:16] Sofia: typically 2-4 weeks once contracts are signed, varies by region and GPU type.
[08:22] Priya: compliance - SOC2 type II, ISO?
[08:25] Marcus: SOC 2 Type II, working on ISO-27001, we can share evidence; that's in the security pack i'll include.
[08:34] [08:38] Sofia: any blockers on your side for a pilot?
[08:41] Ethan: we need the security docs and a sample load script.
[08:44] Samir: and access to a sandbox org so we can create projects and keys.
[08:47] Sofia: we'll provide a sandbox org and a walkthrough with Marcus to run the tests.
[08:51] [09:00] deeper technical Qs - Marcus shows metrics and tracing in console
[09:03] Marcus: per-request traces show model selection, kernel type, and the route selector. you can filter by project key to see token consumption.
[09:12] Dr. Laura: curious about kernel selection - does that change per sequence length?
[09:16] Marcus: yes, the runtime picks kernels and quantization paths depending on seq length and hardware; that's how we optimize latency/cost. sometimes transcription renders "kernel" as "colnel" but that's just the transcript.
[09:28] Priya: for private deployments, can we keep audit logs in our VPC only?
[09:32] Marcus: absolutely; in private deployments logs can stay inside your VPC and never leave.
[09:36] [09:45] closing section
[09:46] Sofia: recap: we'll send the security pack and pricing, spin up a sandbox org, Marcus will run a benchmark plan with Samir, and medivance will provide traffic profiles.
[09:57] Dr. Laura: timeline - can we get the docs by thursday?
[09:59] Sofia: yes, by 2026-04-22.
[10:02] Ethan: can we also get a sample playbook for handling quota breaches?
[10:05] Marcus: yep, include best practices - graceful fallback, backoff strategies, and metrics to track.
[10:11] [10:15] final housekeeping - contact details exchanged, follow-up calendar invites to schedule the benchmark run.
[10:20] Sofia: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and the attachments. bye.
[10:24] Dr. Laura: thanks, bye.

Notes about transcript quality: speaker labels occasionally generic, minor transcription errors ("K V cash" for KV cache, "red wood" vs Redwood). Timestamps approximate every 15-90s.

End of transcript.
